text:
Maya: quick sync — after the release we got two clear signals: a couple enterprise customers flagged higher streaming latency on long sessions, and UX flagged a bunch of small polish items that block adoption. do we do a single mixed squad or split into bug-first + polish later?

Devon: share numbers pls. my gut: bugs first if it impacts SLAs. i can take latency triage but need infra time.

Maya: numbers — Customer X saw 95th latency jump from 200ms -> 420ms on 8k token streams, error rate up 0.8% -> 1.6% during peak windows. not catastrophic but customers are sensitive.

Sasha: +1 bugs-first. polish can be batched into an opt-in micro-release. also want to avoid context switches for infra.

Luis: question — how big is the polish work? are these small CSS/strings or deeper changes?

Maya: mostly copy, a couple UX flows (confirm modal + small animation) and one changeset touching routing logic for fallback CTA. estimate: 3 engineers for 2 days for polish.

Devon: latency fix estimate: need profiling + kernel tweak + a canary — ~5 engineer-days (infra + runtime). if ops-bot can reserve temporary burst capacity we can parallelize.

ops-bot: @Devon requested burst GPU nodes. Reservation created: rsv-1223, 4 nodes, 12h window. :white_check_mark:

Sasha: proposal: 1-week micro-sprint. Day 0-1 triage & triage-cards: label bug:severity=high, assign owners. Day 2-4 fix + canary. Day 5 roll and quick polish pass for any low-effort UX wins.

Maya: sounds good. acceptance criteria for the micro-sprint: 95th latency back within 250ms for 10k token streams under staging load; error rate <0.5%. polish: <5 visible UX issues remaining on the checklist.

Luis: tradeoff question — do we pause other mid-sprint work? my team has a feature branch blocked by runtime changes.

Devon: let's freeze non-critical merges into the serving runtime for the week. allow hotfix branches only.

Maya: decision: freeze runtime merges, spin up bug-squad (Devon lead), quick-polish squad (Sasha lead, 2 devs), ops to monitor canary. I'll update roadmap and tell sales to expect a targeted micro-release end of next week.

Sasha: i'll own the polish checklist and post a short PR template for quick reviews.

Devon: I'll post profiling notes in #eng-runtime and pin the canary instructions:
```
# canary steps
1. deploy rsv-1223 nodes to canary pool
2. route 5% traffic for 2h
3. run perf harness: ./tools/loadgen --tokens 10000 --qps 50
4. collect traces + p95
```

Maya: thanks — i'll update the customer comms doc and add the acceptance criteria to the sprint ticket. @Luis please coordinate QA on canary window. :thumbsup:

Luis: got it — will allocate QA for 2h blocks during canary and post regression notes.

Maya: perfect. next check-in 10:30 tomorrow.

Devon: +1. :rocket:
